change.title: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader
change.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_reader_shard_grants.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- Make the reader's access to shard databases explicit so per-principal
+-- query limits and audit logging apply to it.
+GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader;

verdict.headline: Explicit shard grant for svc_bundle_reader causes worker-runtime startup failure by exceeding max_entries limit
verdict.cause: The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader. The bundle-builder runs as svc_bundle_reader and queries metadata tables. Previously it saw 90 rows from default.* only; with the explicit shard grant it now sees 180 rows (90 from default.* + 90 from r0.*). worker-runtime has max_entries=150 (runtime_config:rc-0013). The candidate experiment (x-871b7056f0fe407b) shows loaded_entries=180 and exit_code=2 ("fatal: bundle has 180 entries but the runtime preallocates 150; refusing to start"). Baseline (x-1d8e89cff28b42b5) shows loaded_entries=90 and exit_code=0. The entry count increase from 90 to 180 exceeds the 150 limit contract, causing worker startup failure.
tested: x-1d8e89cff28b42b5: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-871b7056f0fe407b: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-ef8922b5fd3c48d2: candidate · workload default → failed: runtime_starts_with_bundle
x-d6b15cf47f5e4411: control · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations:
- Only tested with the "default" workload; other workloads may have different limits or data distributions
- The experiment environment may not fully replicate production data volumes or shard configurations
- No measurement of audit logging behavior change with explicit vs implicit grants

mitigation.text: Remove the shard grant GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader and instead create a view on r0 that exposes only the columns needed by bundle-builder, or adjust worker-runtime max_entries limit to >= 180. The minimal change is to either revert the r0.* grant or increase max_entries from 150 to at least 180.

Test candidate: with the explicit shard grant for svc_bundle_reader
Harness confirmation: candidate run required before the judge can call a reproduced failure.
Harness confirmation: control run required before the judge can call a reproduced failure.

hypotheses.claim: The explicit GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader will cause the bundle-builder to query r0.* more broadly, potentially returning rows exceeding the worker-runtime max_entries limit of 150, causing worker startup failure or bundle processing errors.
hypotheses.mechanism: Change adds explicit shard grant to svc_bundle_reader → bundle-builder (running as svc_bundle_reader) can now execute SELECT ON r0.* → bundle-builder queries r0.* for metadata instead of/alongside bundle_fields → increased rows returned → bundle size exceeds worker-runtime max_entries=150 → worker startup failure

hypotheses.claim: The explicit shard grant GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader causes the bundle-builder to see 180 rows (90 from default.* + 90 from r0.*) instead of 90, exceeding worker-runtime max_entries=150 and causing worker startup failure (exit_code 2).
hypotheses.mechanism: Change adds explicit shard grant → bundle-builder (running as svc_bundle_reader) gains access to r0.* → metadata queries return rows from both default and r0 databases → entries count doubles → exceeds max_entries limit 150 → worker-runtime refuses to start
